content.intro: In this lesson, you will study the asperror object and error context as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 47 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: The ASPError Object and Error Context matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Classic ASP exposes request, response, server, session, application, and error objects to scripts. 'The ASPError Object and Error Context' is about choosing the correct object and understanding its lifetime. Query/form values are request-scoped and untrusted; Session is user-specific; Application state is shared by requests and therefore requires concurrency awareness; response headers and redirects must be set before output when required.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Understanding ASP error information; Error numbers and descriptions; Error source information; Error handling boundaries; Using error information for diagnostics; Avoiding the disclosure of internal error details. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: The ASPError Object and Error Context
content_blocks.code:
<%
On Error Resume Next
Call RiskyOperation()
If Err.Number <> 0 Then
  Call LogError(Err.Number, "RiskyOperation")
  Err.Clear
End If
On Error GoTo 0
%>
content_blocks.expected_output: Errors are checked at a narrow boundary and reported through an application-defined logger.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Submit requests through a browser to a local/test IIS site. Test missing fields, repeated parameters, session expiry, and a second request; do not infer security from a successful happy path. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of the asperror object and error context. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.
